subject: social
topic: Your phone's proximity effects your brain's ability to focus on deep tasks
angle: While some experiments and a meta-analysis suggest the mere presence of a smartphone reduces cognitive capacity or working memory, a larger meta-analysis found no significant effect on cognitive outcomes.
title: The Cost of Proximity

hooks.text: Does your phone drain your brain when it is silent?
You do not touch your phone, yet it still affects your focus.
Your smartphone dependence is costing you cognitive capacity.
A phone sits face down on a wooden desk.
Cognitive costs are highest for those with high smartphone dependence.

reveal.headline: The mere presence of a phone reduces your cognitive capacity.
reveal.body: Even if you do not touch the device, it occupies your mental resources. The evidence on this is mixed, however, as some larger studies find no significant effect.

explain.headline: The cost of proximity.
explain.body: A smartphone nearby can drain your working memory. This effect is most pronounced for people with a high level of smartphone dependence. For others, the impact may be negligible.

matters.headline: The invisible drain.
matters.body: That may be why you feel less focused when your phone is on the desk. Your brain may be constantly calculating the possibility of a notification.

example.headline: The desk on your table.
example.body: You sit down to write a report. Your phone sits face down next to your laptop. You feel a slight tension in your focus as you work.

question.headline: Where does your attention go when your phone is in the room?

claims.text: The mere presence of a smartphone reduces available cognitive capacity, even when people successfully avoid checking the device.
claims.quote: even when people are successful at maintaining sustained attention—as when avoiding the temptation to check their phones—the mere presence of these devices reduces available cognitive capacity.

claims.text: A meta-analysis found that the mere presence of a smartphone negatively impacts working memory capacity, but has no significant effect on other cognitive functions.
claims.quote: Working memory capacity was negatively impacted by the mere presence of a smartphone, while results for the remaining cognitive functions produced null summary effects.

claims.text: Participants with higher positive urgency showed more cognitive interference in a silent-mode smartphone condition compared to a turned-off smartphone condition.
claims.quote: The results showed that participants with higher positive urgency presented increased cognitive interference (reflected by poorer task performance) in the "silent-mode smartphone" condition compared with participants in the "turned-off smartphone" condition.

claims.text: The cognitive costs of a smartphone's presence are highest for people who have a high level of smartphone dependence.
claims.quote: Moreover, these cognitive costs are highest for those highest in smartphone dependence.

claims.text: In an experiment with participants aged 20-34, the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance.
claims.quote: The results of the conducted experiment imply that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance, which supports the hypothesis of the smartphone presence using limited cognitive resources.

verdict: The evidence is mixed, with some studies showing a 'brain drain' effect on working memory and cognitive capacity while others find no statistically significant impact.
caveat: The research is characterized by substantial methodological heterogeneity and generally poor statistical power.
caption:
Your phone may be draining your brain even when it is silent. 

Research shows that the mere presence of a smartphone can reduce cognitive capacity and working memory, though results are mixed and often lack statistical power. 

Does your phone feel like a weight on your focus?
